doctrine: FASHION_KILLA is a compilation of Reddit posts and YouTube video transcripts on men's fashion basics. Core themes: fit is paramount (90% of style problems solved by proper fit); neutral color palettes (white, black, navy, olive, grey, khaki, brown) are foundational; quality over quantity; occasion-appropriate dressing; understanding face shapes and body types for hat/clothing selection; accessories as statement pieces (watches, belts, rings, sunglasses); layering and texture add depth; grooming and confidence are non-negotiable; avoid logos/graphics for mature appearance; classic styles beat trends; build wardrobes slowly and intentionally. Key frameworks: Light-Dark Rule (contrast tops/bottoms), 3-Color Rule (limit colors per outfit), Pareto's Principle (20% of wardrobe gets 80% use), The Swap Trick (gradual style introduction), Pull-3 shopping trick. Specific garment recommendations: white sneakers, dark jeans, chinos, loafers, plain t-shirts, oxford shirts, cardigans, blazers, tailored trousers, leather jackets, overcoats. Hat guidance: baseball caps, beanies, trucker hats, fedoras, flat caps (face-shape dependent); brim bend vs. flat; sizing critical. No em-dashes used throughout.
workflows: Slow wardrobe build: find style > measure body > buy basics > layer intentionally > add personality
Outfit composition: start neutral base > add one statement piece > balance with accessories > verify face-shape appropriateness
Color coordination: choose top/bottom contrast > add maximum 3 colors > match belt to shoes > use neutrals as default
Shopping routine: measure yourself > Pull 3 sizes > check fit in mirror > ask for feedback > return if unsure
prompts: What colors complement your skin tone?
Does this occasion require dressing up or down?
Is the fit flattering for your body type?
Can you wear this piece 5+ different ways?
Does this match your established style identity?
operating_rules: Invest in basics first, personality pieces second
One statement piece per outfit maximum
Accessories carry the most personal expression
Quality items last longer and compound style
Hat style depends on face shape and head size
content_ideas: Fit troubleshooting for different body types
Thrifting and vintage hunting best practices
contradictions: Skipping graphic tees for maturity vs. some recommendations include vintage graphic tees in proper styling
Tight vs. loose fit debate (skinny jeans discouraged but slim-fit praised)

Designer accessories necessary for status vs. budget options work equally well
weird_gold: The 90% rule: proper fit solves 90% of style problems
The Swap Trick: introduce one clothing element at a time to test comfort
Pull-3 shopping: always try one size up and one down
Break-in outfit ritual: wear new pieces for errands before special events
Wabisabi principle: embrace worn-in, lived-in aesthetic
The 3% rule: subtle details (mandarin collar, dropped crotch) differentiate basics
Ma concept: negative space and minimalism are design principles
Shokunin spirit: obsessive craftsmanship justifies premium pricing
Museum-as-wardrobe: clothes document your life story through wear patterns
